judge_panel.reason: Table 1 shows entries where f_MM is reported as exactly 0 (e.g., rows (41-44), (47-50), (55-60), (60-65)) yet Z_MM takes non-zero negative values (-0.931, -0.636, -0.636, -0.505). The paper states it 'clamp[s] the MM pseudo-intensity to zero if the value fluctuates below the baseline ratio' and defines Z_MM = I_MM/sigma_I_MM, so if I_MM is clamped to zero, Z_MM should also be zero, not negative—this is a genuine internal inconsistency in how the clamping is applied relative to the reported significance values.

The paper explicitly states it will "clamp the MM pseudo-intensity to zero if the value fluctuates below the baseline ratio to avoid negative values" and then defines "Z_MM = I_MM/\sigma_{I_MM}." But Table 1 reports bins with "f_MM = 0" and negative significances, e.g. "(41–44) 0  -0.931" and "(47–50) 0  -0.636," which is inconsistent with the stated clamping of I_MM.

The paper explicitly defines $Z_{MM} = f_{MM} / \sigma_{f_{MM}}$ on page 6, yet Table 1 reports negative non-zero values for $Z_{MM}$ (e.g., -0.931) in rows where $f_{MM}$ is clamped to 0, confirming the reviewer's claim of inconsistent application of the non-negativity constraint.
